subject: Potential data exposure — request for IRP & evidence
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@rivermark.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@rivermark.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure observed Apr 11 — needs IRP + evidence

Hannah,

We observed unexpected request traces in our ingestion logs this morning that appear to contain short snippets of user-entered text from a small subset of sandbox tenants. The traces include user identifiers and brief message fragments. At this time we do not have evidence of bulk exfiltration, but the presence of identifiable snippets is concerning and we need help triaging.

What we can share immediately: a small redacted log snippet and request metadata for three sample requests (attached). We are requesting:
- Confirmation this data could have originated from Redwood’s API stack (yes/no)
- A copy of your IR plan (high level) and a timeline of actions you will take
- Any in-flight mitigations you can apply now (rate-limits, token revocation, temporary blocklists)
- A compact evidence bundle (logs, request IDs, timestamps) for our audit team

Our contact for the investigation is Tom Ellis (secops) and we can provide a secured SFTP if you prefer.

Attached: sample-request-log-snippet.txt (redacted)

Please let me know how you want to proceed and who on your side will lead the investigation. This is time-sensitive for our compliance team.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Lead, Security Operations
RiverMark Bank
security@rivermark.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@rivermark.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure observed Apr 11 — needs IRP + evidence

Tom — thanks for the quick heads up and for the snippet. We’re treating this as an incident and I’ll be your primary contact from Redwood.

Immediate actions we are initiating now:
- Sean (cc’d) will run a focused request-ID search across the ingestion tier and the request-forwarding proxy to identify any matching traces.
- We will temporarily pause ingestion for the three tenant IDs you included (if you confirm the tenant IDs) to prevent further writes while we investigate.
- We’ll start building an evidence bundle (redacted logs, request IDs, headers, and timestamps) and provide a secure transfer method.

Please confirm whether you want the bundle uploaded to your SFTP or shared via an encrypted Drive link. Also please share the tenant IDs in the redacted file (if not present) so we can scope quickly.

I’m attaching a one-line acknowledgement for your compliance team (initial-ack.txt). We’ll aim to provide an interim triage report within 4 hours and a remediation/update cadence after that.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@rivermark.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure observed Apr 11 — needs IRP + evidence

Tom / Hannah — quick triage summary and next steps (high level):

1) Scope: using the sample-request-log-snippet I ran targeted queries across the gateway and request-collector pods. I’ve identified 7 request IDs spanning 2027-04-11 02:43:12Z through 2027-04-11 03:07:51Z that match the pattern in the snippet. Early signs point to a misapplied ingestion routing rule created during a recent onboarding sync — that rule allowed a small set of sandbox tenants to route via a shared proxy that was mis-tagging certain headers.

2) Immediate mitigations applied (completed):
- Blocked the suspect routing rule in control plane (temporary revert)
- Rotated the short-lived proxy tokens for the affected pool
- Temporarily suspended ingestion for the three sandbox tenant IDs listed in your snippet (once you confirm)

3) Evidence we will provide in the bundle:
- Redacted request logs for the 7 request IDs (gateway + collector)
- Proxy header dumps and our internal routing configuration at the time
- Timeline of changes and operator actions (control-plane audit)

4) Next steps / ETA:
- Interim triage note to you in 4 hours (we’re on that)
- Full evidence bundle and a short-form postmortem within 7 business days
- Offer to run a joint forensics call if RiverMark wants to review artifacts together

If you prefer an immediate SFTP transfer, provide credentials. Otherwise I’ll stage the bundle on an encrypted Drive folder and share access.

—Sean
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@rivermark.com>, security@rivermark.com
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RiverMark incident: post-incident summary, evidence bundle, and SOC2/SIG mapping

Tom / RiverMark security team —

Thank you for your patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is a compact evidence package and a short post-incident summary. This message is intended to close the loop on the operational facts and provide the artifacts your audit team requested.

Summary (short):
- Root cause: A recently-applied onboarding sync (operator error in a scripted config push) created a routing alias that caused three sandbox tenants to be routed through a shared proxy pool without the intended header sanitization. That proxy appended a diagnostic header that, in rare cases, duplicated a short user-submitted text fragment into an auxiliary log field. No backend data store was exposed. The exposure was limited to transient logs in a short retention buffer.
- Impact: 7 request traces contained brief identifiable snippets from sandbox tenants. No indication of automated exfiltration or access to production customer data.
- Actions taken: Reverted the onboarding sync, removed the routing alias, rotated proxy tokens, revoked affected short-lived tokens, and tightened header-sanitization checks in the gateway.
- Remediation verification: We ran targeted replay tests and verified sanitized headers for the affected paths.

What we’ve attached: rmk-ir-evidence-bundle-20270418.zip (redacted logs and timeline), forensics-summary-20270418.pdf (2-page summary), and an index file listing included artifacts.

SOC2 / SIG mapping:
We mapped the evidence to relevant SOC2 criteria and SIG control families. If you’d like, Neha (cc’d) will provide a succinct matrix that links specific artifacts to control IDs.

Share method: evidence bundle is available in an encrypted Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1example-rivermark-ir-evidence (access granted to the security@rivermark.com group). Jira ticket created for internal tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-8429

Offer: we can host a 45-minute walkthrough with our forensics lead and a member of your audit team to go over artifacts and the SIG crosswalk. Would Thu or Fri (Apr 21/22) work for a call?

If you need additional redaction or an expanded artifact set (e.g., full control-plane audit logs under an NDA), tell us and we’ll route the request through our legal/compliance channels.

Thanks again — we treat these issues seriously and appreciate RiverMark’s partnership on a careful review.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: rmk-ir-evidence-bundle-20270418.zip (redacted), forensics-summary-20270418.pdf, index.txt
